content.user_title: Build with Next.js App Router Patterns
content.value_statement: Next.js projects can become inconsistent when routes, client components, and data fetching follow different conventions. This skill provides concise project-focused guidance for App Router structure, navigation, fetching, fonts, and metadata.
actual_capabilities: Explains App Router page and layout file locations.
Guides when to use Client Components or Server Components.
Recommends Link and useRouter for navigation.
Describes server-side and client-side data-fetching approaches.
Covers next/font usage and metadata placement.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not modify project files.
It does not cover Pages Router migration details.
It does not provide authentication, caching, or database implementation patterns.
Its recommendations reflect the documented project conventions.

use_cases.title: Create a route page
use_cases.description: Choose the correct App Router file location and component type for a new page.

use_cases.title: Review component boundaries
use_cases.description: Decide whether a component needs client-side state or can remain a Server Component.

use_cases.title: Standardize project conventions
use_cases.description: Apply consistent navigation, font, and metadata practices across a Next.js codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Start a page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Next.js Patterns guidance to explain where I should create a dashboard page and whether it should be a Server Component.

prompt_templates.title: Choose navigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this navigation requirement and recommend whether I should use Link or useRouter, with a short explanation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan data fetching
prompt_templates.prompt: Using these patterns, recommend a data-fetching approach for a Server Component and identify when client-side fetching is appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Review an App Router feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess my proposed App Router feature against the documented patterns for routes, layouts, client boundaries, navigation, fonts, and metadata.

output_examples.input: Where should I add a profile route?
output: Use a Server Component unless the page needs browser APIs or interactive state.

output_examples.input: How should users navigate to the settings page?
output: Use Link for a normal internal navigation element.
Use useRouter only when navigation must occur after an interaction or condition.

output_examples.input: Where should page metadata be defined?
output_examples.output: Define metadata in the relevant page.tsx or layout.tsx file for the route.

best_practices: Default to Server Components and add use client only when browser features or state are required.
Use Link for standard internal navigation and reserve useRouter for programmatic navigation.
Define route metadata close to the relevant page or layout.
anti_patterns: Do not mark every component as a Client Component without a browser-specific need.
Do not use useRouter when a regular Link provides the required navigation.
Do not place unrelated route metadata in a distant file.

faq.question: What routing system does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers the Next.js App Router and its app directory conventions.

faq.question: When should I use use client?
faq.answer: Use it when a component needs state, effects, event-driven browser APIs, or client-only hooks.

faq.question: When should I use Link?
faq.answer: Use Link for standard navigation between internal application routes.

faq.question: When should I use useRouter?
faq.answer: Use useRouter for programmatic navigation triggered by application logic or user actions.

faq.question: Can Server Components fetch data?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill recommends fetching data directly in Server Components when appropriate.

faq.question: Does this skill implement the patterns?
faq.answer: No. It supplies guidance and does not create, modify, or execute project code.
